ukberi-tibyan:1-1.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لَمْ يَكُنِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ وَالْمُشْرِكِينَ مُنْفَكِّينَ حَتَّى تَأْتِيَهُمُ الْبَيِّنَةُ (١)).
The words of the Exalted (وَالْمُشْرِكِينَ): it is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to «أَهْلِ». (مُنْفَكِّينَ) is the khabar (predicate) of «كَانَ». (مِنْ أَهْلِ) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) in «كَفَرُوا».

ukberi-tibyan:2-3.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (رَسُولٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ يَتْلُو صُحُفًا مُطَهَّرَةً (٢) فِيهَا كُتُبٌ قَيِّمَةٌ (٣)).
The words of the Exalted (رَسُولٌ): it is a badal (substitute) for «الْبَيِّنَةُ», or the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject).
(مِنَ اللَّهِ) may be a ṣifa (adjective) of «رَسُولٌ», or attached (mutaʿalliq) to it.
(يَتْلُو) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in the preposition phrase, or a ṣifa of (رَسُولٌ).
It is also possible for «مِنَ اللَّهِ» to be a ḥāl from «صُحُفًا», i.e. he recites purified scriptures sent down from Allah.
(فِيهَا كُتُبٌ): the clause is a naʿt (adjective) of «صُحُف».

ukberi-tibyan:5-5.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَا أُمِرُوا إِلَّا لِيَعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ الدِّينَ حُنَفَاءَ وَيُقِيمُوا الصَّلَاةَ وَيُؤْتُوا الزَّكَاةَ وَذَلِكَ دِينُ الْقَيِّمَةِ (٥)).
(مُخْلِصِينَ) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «يَعْبُدُوا». (حُنَفَاءَ) is another ḥāl, or a ḥāl from the pronoun in «مُخْلِصِينَ».
The words of the Exalted (دِينُ الْقَيِّمَةِ): that is, of the upright creed (milla) or the upright community (umma).

ukberi-tibyan:6-6.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ وَالْمُشْرِكِينَ فِي نَارِ جَهَنَّمَ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا أُولَئِكَ هُمْ شَرُّ الْبَرِيَّةِ (٦)).
The words of the Exalted (فِي نَارِ جَهَنَّمَ): it is the khabar (predicate) of «إِنَّ».
(خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in the khabar.
(الْبَرِيَّةِ) is without hamza in the widespread usage, though its origin is with hamza, from «بَرَأَ اللَّهُ الْخَلْقَ» (Allah created the creation), i.e. originated it. It is of the pattern «فَعِيلَة» in the sense of «مَفْعُولَة», and it is an adjective that has come to be used as a noun (ṣifa ghāliba), because the qualified noun is [not] mentioned with it. [Translator's note: the printed text reads «لِأَنَّهَا يُذْكَرُ مَعَهَا الْمَوْصُوفُ» ("because the qualified noun is mentioned with it"); the sense of ṣifa ghāliba requires "is not mentioned", so a negation seems to have dropped out. The pattern is also printed as «مُفَعْوِلَة», evidently for «مَفْعُولَة».]
It is said that whoever does not pronounce it with hamza takes it from «الْبَرَى», which is earth (dust). Some have read it with hamza, according to the original form.

ukberi-tibyan:8-8.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (جَزَاؤُهُمْ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ جَنَّاتُ عَدْنٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا أَبَدًا رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ وَرَضُوا عَنْهُ ذَلِكَ لِمَنْ خَشِيَ رَبَّهُ (٨)).
The words of the Exalted (خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا): it is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and the governor (ʿāmil) in it is omitted, its implied form being: «ادْخُلُوهَا خَالِدِينَ» (enter it, abiding forever), or «أُعْطَوْهَا» (they were given it). It cannot be a ḥāl from the genitive pronoun in «جَزَاؤُهُمْ», because if you said that, you would separate the maṣdar (verbal noun) from what it governs by the khabar (predicate). Some allowed it, arguing that the maṣdar here is not to be construed as «أَنْ» plus the verb; but this is far-fetched. As for «عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ», it may be an adverbial (ẓarf) for «جَزَاؤُهُمْ», or a ḥāl from it.
(أَبَدًا) is an adverbial of time (ẓarf zamān). And Allah knows best.
